Across 3 accepted bundles, 0 of 8 counter-authority rows entered through any retrieval channel the initial broad pass did not use. Re-verified byte-identically in runs 38794235870, 38797568256 and 38799078780: no bundle declares or logs an adversarial retrieval stage (stage inventories are exactly ['search','lang','leading','citations'] on all three bundles; channel vocabulary closed on all three provenance-carrying bundles; the four frozen legs carry no retrieval provenance and report NOT_APPLICABLE_NO_PROVENANCE rather than a vacuous negative), and none of the 4 counter-authority mechanisms the accepted tree ships can reach a decision outside the initial pool. The accepted AdversarialPass still sees a deterministic 24-decision shortlist, leaving 89.4% / 91.6% / 76.0% of the retrieved corpus structurally uninspected.
operational_note: Run 38794235870 diagnosed a workflow defect: .github/workflows/frontier-team.yml's 'Validate Frontier producer delta and state' step infers 'durable delta' from the ABSENCE of a clean tree and never consults git log, so a producer that commits its own work is failed with exit 67 AFTER its work is already durable, and the resilience job then re-dispatches the same charter. .github/** is outside this team's write scope, so it is reported, not patched. This run therefore leaves its delta UNCOMMITTED in the working tree, which is what that guard inspects; the workflow's 'Persist team snapshot' step commits it afterwards. A further re-dispatch of this charter after this run is therefore a control-plane symptom, not missing work.
